text:
sam: Quick check — we've been shipping a debug log that includes full LLM responses for a small percentage of requests. I noticed entries like:

{ user_id: 123, prompt: "Summarize invoice for alice@example.com", response: "...Alice owes $1,234.56...", raw_tokens: "..." }

Is that allowed or do we need to scrub more aggressively before it hits logs? cc @maria for privacy rules

maria: We should not persist PII (emails, SSNs, payment info). Responses can contain PII from user content — scrub before storage. For short-term debug traces we can keep ephemeral logs but they must be redacted and TTLed. See policy: https://redwood.internal/docs/privacy/logging

sam: Got it. Current pipeline calls telemetry.log('llm_debug', payload) — should we drop user_id and prompt completely or pseudonymize?

jordan: Pseudonymize user_id (hash with HMAC) is fine for correlating, but drop or redact prompts that include emails/phones. For responses, run the redactor step that replaces emails/phones/cc numbers with <REDACTED>. Example regex we use in scrubber:

```js
const EMAIL = /[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}/ig
const CC = /(?:4[0-9]{12}(?:[0-9]{3})?|5[1-5][0-9]{14})/g
payload.response = payload.response.replace(EMAIL, '<REDACTED_EMAIL>').replace(CC, '<REDACTED_CC>')
```

maria: Also remove raw_tokens and any full prompt text from long-term stores. If you need to keep prompt hashes for debugging, store HMAC(prompt) + reason tag.

lee: Ops note — if you start TTLing logs, update retention policy and make sure splunk/elastic index templates won't keep a copy. @ops-bot can help auto-delete after 7 days for this debug index.

ops-bot: scheduled deletion enabled for index llm-debug-ephemeral, TTL=7d (requested by lee).

sam: Perfect. I'll open a tiny PR to add the scrub step into the telemetry pipeline and HMAC user_id. Will include unit tests and a flag to enable for the rollout.

jordan: LGTY — add an integration test that verifies <REDACTED_EMAIL> appears and no raw_tokens field persists.

maria: Ping me on the PR for a quick privacy review. If any customer data could be sensitive, we escalate to legal.

sam: Thanks all, patch incoming. :thumbsup:
